title: Sep 22 Results + Sep 23 Preview: 60% Looks Good Until You See What We Left on the Table
summary: 9-6 record sounds solid, but let's talk about those six misses that shouldn't have happened.

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: 60% Isn't Something to Celebrate

Sure, 9-6 sounds respectable. Sure, 60% is above .500. But you know what? When I look at these six losses, I see missed opportunities written all over them. We went 9-6 on September 22nd, and while the math nerds are celebrating, I'm asking the hard questions nobody wants to hear.

## The Brutal Truth About Yesterday

Let's talk about what actually happened. We nailed the Pirates, hit on the Guardians, caught the White Sox upset over the Royals. That's the good news. The bad news? We whiffed on BOTH Rays-Yankees games in the worst way possible, got embarrassed by the Tigers at home, and completely botched the Cubs call at 61% confidence. That Cubs miss? That one stings because when you're that confident and still wrong, you've got problems.

## Here's My Hot Take Nobody Asked For

The Mets-Rangers pick at 50%? That was basically a coin flip and we shouldn't have pushed it. The Braves miss at 51%? Same story. But when you're at 61-62% confidence and getting burned, that's when you need to look in the mirror. The Tigers and Cubs losses weren't close calls—they were straight-up wrong reads of the situation.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Can We Actually Deliver?

Speaking of the Tigers—yeah, they embarrassed us yesterday. So what do we do? We're going RIGHT BACK to them on September 23rd. Nationals at Tigers, and we're taking Detroit at 61% confidence. Some might call this revenge betting. I call it recognizing that Framber Valdez on the mound against Richard Lovelady isn't even a fair fight.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 23 Top Pick
content.sub: 61% Win Probability • Valdez vs Lovelady • Tigers at Home

content.value:
## The Controversial Truth About This Pick

Let me be brutally honest: betting on the Tigers after they just made us look foolish yesterday takes guts—or stupidity. I haven't decided which. But Framber Valdez is an ace-caliber arm, and the Nationals are sending out Richard Lovelady, who—let's just say—doesn't exactly strike fear into opposing lineups.

The model says 61%. Yesterday it said 62% on the Tigers and we face-planted. But you know what separates winners from losers? Short memory and conviction. The matchup is there. The numbers are there. The only question is whether we have the stones to trust it after getting burned.

**My prediction? Tigers roll.** And if I'm wrong twice in a row on Detroit, I'll write a formal apology. But I won't be wrong.
